model.dbt_artifacts.dim_dbt__current_mod.raw_code:
with
    base as (select * from {{ ref("stg_dbt__models") }}),
    model_executions as (select * from {{ ref("stg_dbt__model_executions") }}),
    latest_models as (

        /* Retrieves the models present in the most recent run */
        select * from base where run_started_at = (select max(run_started_at) from base)

    ),

    latest_models_runs as (

        /* Retreives all successful run information for the models present in the most
        recent run and ranks them based on query completion time */
        select
            model_executions.node_id,
            model_executions.was_full_refresh,
            model_executions.query_completed_at,
            model_executions.total_node_runtime,
            model_executions.rows_affected
            {% if target.type == "bigquery" %}, model_executions.bytes_processed {% endif %},
            /* Row number by refresh and node ID */
            row_number() over (
                partition by latest_models.node_id, model_executions.was_full_refresh
                order by model_executions.query_completed_at desc  /* most recent ranked first */
            ) as run_idx,
            /* Row number by node ID */
            row_number() over (
                partition by latest_models.node_id order by model_executions.query_completed_at desc  /* most recent ranked first */
            ) as run_idx_id_only
        from model_executions
        inner join latest_models on model_executions.node_id = latest_models.node_id
        where model_executions.status = 'success'

    ),

    latest_model_stats as (

        select
            node_id,
            max(
                case
                    when was_full_refresh {% if target.type == "sqlserver" %} = 1 {% endif %}
                    then query_completed_at
                end
            ) as last_full_refresh_run_completed_at,
            max(
                case
                    when was_full_refresh {% if target.type == "sqlserver" %} = 1 {% endif %}
                    then total_node_runtime
                end
            ) as last_full_refresh_run_total_runtime,
            max(
                case
                    when was_full_refresh {% if target.type == "sqlserver" %} = 1 {% endif %}
                    then rows_affected
                end
            ) as last_full_refresh_run_rows_affected
            {% if target.type == "bigquery" %}
                ,
                max(
                    case when was_full_refresh then bytes_processed end
                ) as last_full_refresh_run_bytes_processed
            {% endif %},
            max(case when run_idx_id_only = 1 then query_completed_at end) as last_run_completed_at,
            max(
                case when run_idx_id_only = 1 then total_node_runtime end
            ) as last_run_total_runtime,
            max(case when run_idx_id_only = 1 then rows_affected end) as last_run_rows_affected
            {% if target.type == "bigquery" %}
                ,
                max(
                    case when run_idx_id_only = 1 then bytes_processed end
                ) as last_run_bytes_processed
            {% endif %},
            max(
                case
                    when not was_full_refresh {% if target.type == "sqlserver" %} = 1 {% endif %}
                    then query_completed_at
                end
            ) as last_incremental_run_completed_at,
            max(
                case
                    when not was_full_refresh {% if target.type == "sqlserver" %} = 1 {% endif %}
                    then total_node_runtime
                end
            ) as last_incremental_run_total_runtime,
            max(
                case
                    when not was_full_refresh {% if target.type == "sqlserver" %} = 1 {% endif %}
                    then rows_affected
                end
            ) as last_incremental_run_rows_affected
            {% if target.type == "bigquery" %}
                ,
                max(
                    case when not was_full_refresh then bytes_processed end
                ) as last_incremental_run_bytes_processed
            {% endif %}
        from latest_models_runs
        where run_idx = 1
        group by node_id

    ),

    final as (

        select
            latest_models.*,
            latest_model_stats.last_full_refresh_run_completed_at,
            latest_model_stats.last_full_refresh_run_total_runtime,
            latest_model_stats.last_full_refresh_run_rows_affected
            {% if target.type == "bigquery" %}
                , latest_model_stats.last_full_refresh_run_bytes_processed
            {% endif %},
            latest_model_stats.last_run_completed_at,
            latest_model_stats.last_run_total_runtime,
            latest_model_stats.last_run_rows_affected
            {% if target.type == "bigquery" %}
                , latest_model_stats.last_run_bytes_processed
            {% endif %},
            latest_model_stats.last_incremental_run_completed_at,
            latest_model_stats.last_incremental_run_total_runtime,
            latest_model_stats.last_incremental_run_rows_affected
            {% if target.type == "bigquery" %}
                , latest_model_stats.last_incremental_run_bytes_processed
            {% endif %}
        from latest_models
        left join latest_model_stats on latest_models.node_id = latest_model_stats.node_id

    )

select *
from final

with all_relationships as (

        *
    from {{ ref('int_all_dag_relationships') }}
    where distance <> 0
    and parent_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
    and child_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
),

final as (
    select
        parent,
        child, -- the model with potentially long run time / compilation time, improve performance by breaking the upstream chain of views
        distance,
        path
    from all_relationships
    where is_dependent_on_chain_of_views = cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
    and child_resource_type = 'model'
    and distance > {{ var('chained_views_threshold') }}
)

select * from final

{{ filter_exceptions() }}

model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_direct_j.raw_code:
-- this model finds cases where a model has a reference to both a model and a source

with direct_model_relationships as (
    select  
        *
    from {{ ref('int_all_dag_relationships') }}
    where child_resource_type = 'model'
    and distance = 1
    and parent_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
    and child_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
),

model_and_source_joined as (
    select
        child,
        case
            when (
                sum(case when parent_resource_type = 'model' then 1 else 0 end) > 0
                and sum(case when parent_resource_type = 'source' then 1 else 0 end) > 0
            )
            then cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
            else cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
        end as keep_row 
    from direct_model_relationships
    group by child
),

final as (
    select
        direct_model_relationships.parent,
        direct_model_relationships.parent_resource_type,
        direct_model_relationships.child,
        direct_model_relationships.child_resource_type,
        direct_model_relationships.distance
    from direct_model_relationships
    inner join model_and_source_joined
        on direct_model_relationships.child = model_and_source_joined.child
    where model_and_source_joined.keep_row = cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
)

select * from final

{{ filter_exceptions() }}
order by child

model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_model_di.name: fct_model_directories
model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_model_di.description: This finds all cases where a model is NOT in the appropriate subdirectory.
model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_model_di.raw_code:
-- This model finds all cases where a model is NOT in the appropriate subdirectory:
    -- For staging models: The files should be in nested in the staging folder in a subfolder that matches their source parent's name.
    -- For non-staging models: The files should be nested closest to their appropriate folder.  
{% set directory_pattern = get_directory_pattern() %}
 
with all_graph_resources as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_all_graph_resources') }}
    where is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
),

folders as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_naming_convention_folders') }}
), 

all_dag_relationships as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_all_dag_relationships') }}
    where child_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
),

staging_models as (
    select  
        child,
        child_resource_type,
        child_model_type,
        child_file_path,
        child_directory_path,
        child_file_name,
        parent_source_name
    from all_dag_relationships
    where parent_resource_type = 'source'
    and child_resource_type = 'model'
    and child_model_type = 'staging'
),

-- find all staging models that are NOT in their source parent's subdirectory
inappropriate_subdirectories_staging as (
    select distinct -- must do distinct to avoid duplicates when staging model has multiple paths to a given source
        child as resource_name,
        child_resource_type as resource_type,
        child_model_type as model_type,
        child_file_path as current_file_path,
        {{ dbt.concat(["'models" ~ directory_pattern ~ "'", "'" ~ var("staging_folder_name") ~ "'", "'" ~ directory_pattern ~ "'", 'parent_source_name', "'" ~ directory_pattern ~ "'", 'child_file_name']) }} as change_file_path_to
    from staging_models
    where child_directory_path not like {{ dbt.concat(["'%'", 'parent_source_name', "'%'"]) }}
),

-- find all non-staging models that are NOT nested closest to their appropriate folder
innappropriate_subdirectories_non_staging_models as (
    select 
        all_graph_resources.resource_name,
        all_graph_resources.resource_type,
        all_graph_resources.model_type,
        all_graph_resources.file_path as current_file_path,
        {{ dbt.concat(["'models'", "'" ~ directory_pattern ~ "..." ~ directory_pattern ~ "'", 'folders.folder_name_value', "'" ~ directory_pattern ~ "..." ~ directory_pattern ~ "'", 'all_graph_resources.file_name']) }} as change_file_path_to
    from all_graph_resources
    left join folders 
        on folders.model_type = all_graph_resources.model_type 
    -- either appropriate folder_name is not in the current_directory_path or a inappropriate folder name is closer to the file_name
    where all_graph_resources.model_type <> all_graph_resources.model_type_folder 
),

unioned as (
    select * from inappropriate_subdirectories_staging
    union all
    select * from innappropriate_subdirectories_non_staging_models
)

select * from unioned

{{ filter_exceptions() }}

model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_model_fa.name: fct_model_fanout
model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_model_fa.description: This table shows all parents with more direct leaf children than the threshold for fanout (determined by variable models_fanout_threshold, default 3)
model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_model_fa.raw_code:
with all_dag_relationships as (
    select
        *
    from {{ ref('int_all_dag_relationships') }}
    where parent_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
    and child_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
),

-- find all models without children
models_without_children as (
    select
        parent
    from all_dag_relationships
    where parent_resource_type = 'model'
    group by parent
    having max(distance) = 0
),

-- all parents with more direct children than the threshold for fanout (determined by variable models_fanout_threshold, default 3)
    -- Note: only counts "leaf children" - direct chilren that are models AND are child-less (are at the right-most-point in the DAG)
model_fanout as (
    select 
        all_dag_relationships.parent,
        all_dag_relationships.parent_model_type,
        all_dag_relationships.child
    from all_dag_relationships
    inner join models_without_children
        on all_dag_relationships.child = models_without_children.parent

model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_rejoinin.name: fct_rejoining_of_upstream_concepts
model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_rejoinin.description: "All cases where one of the parent's direct children (child) is ALSO the direct child of ANOTHER one of the  parent's direct children (parent_and_child). Only includes cases where the model "in between" the parent and child  has NO other downstream dependencies.
model.dbt_project_evaluator.fct_rejoinin.raw_code:
with all_relationships as (
    select  
        *
    from {{ ref('int_all_dag_relationships') }}
    where parent_resource_type not in ('exposure', 'metric')
    and child_resource_type not in ('exposure', 'metric')
    and parent_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
    and child_is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
),

-- all parent/child relationships where the parent is BOTH the direct parent of the child and the second level parent of the child 
rejoined as (
    select
        parent,
        child
    from all_relationships
    group by parent, child
    having (sum(case when distance = 1 then 1 else 0 end) >= 1
        and sum(case when distance = 2 then 1 else 0 end) >= 1)
),

-- resources with only one direct child
single_use_resources as (
    select
        parent
    from all_relationships
    where distance = 1
    group by parent
    having count(*) = 1
),

-- all cases where one of the parent's direct children (child) is ALSO the direct child of ANOTHER one of the parent's direct childen (parent_and_child)
triad_relationships as (
    select 
        rejoined.parent,
        rejoined.child,
        direct_child.parent as parent_and_child
    from rejoined
    left join all_relationships as direct_child
        on rejoined.child = direct_child.child
        and direct_child.distance = 1
    left join all_relationships as direct_parent
        on rejoined.parent = direct_parent.parent
        and direct_parent.distance = 1
    where direct_child.parent = direct_parent.child
),

-- additionally, only includes cases where the model "in between" the parent and parent_and_child has NO other downstream dependencies
-- Note: when the "in between" model DOES have downstream dependencies, it's possible this DAG choice has been made to avoid duplicated code and as such is OKAY
final as (
    select
        triad_relationships.*,
        case
            when single_use_resources.parent is not null then cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
            else cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
        end as is_loop_independent
    from triad_relationships
    left join single_use_resources 
        on triad_relationships.parent_and_child = single_use_resources.parent
),

final_filtered as (
    select * from final
    where is_loop_independent = cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
)

select * from final_filtered

model.dbt_project_evaluator.int_direct_r.raw_code:
-- one record for each resource in the graph and its direct parent
with

all_graph_resources as (
    select
        resource_id,
        resource_name,
        resource_type,
        file_path,
        directory_path,
        file_name,
        model_type,
        materialized,
        is_public,
        access,
        source_name,
        is_excluded
    from {{ ref('int_all_graph_resources') }}
),

direct_model_relationships as (
    select
        resource_id,
        direct_parent_id,
        is_primary_relationship
    from {{ ref('stg_node_relationships')}}
),

direct_exposure_relationships as (
    select
        resource_id,
        direct_parent_id,
        is_primary_relationship
    from {{ ref('stg_exposure_relationships')}}
),

direct_metrics_relationships as (
    select
        resource_id,
        direct_parent_id,
        is_primary_relationship
    from {{ ref('stg_metric_relationships')}}
),

-- for all resources in the graph, find their direct parent
direct_relationships as (
    select
        all_graph_resources.resource_id as resource_id,
        all_graph_resources.resource_name as resource_name,
        all_graph_resources.resource_type as resource_type,
        all_graph_resources.file_path as file_path,
        all_graph_resources.directory_path as directory_path,
        all_graph_resources.file_name as file_name,
        all_graph_resources.model_type as model_type,
        all_graph_resources.materialized as materialized,
        all_graph_resources.is_public as is_public,
        all_graph_resources.access as access,
        all_graph_resources.source_name as source_name,
        all_graph_resources.is_excluded as is_excluded,
        case
            when all_graph_resources.resource_type = 'source' then null
            when all_graph_resources.resource_type = 'exposure' then exposures.direct_parent_id
            when all_graph_resources.resource_type = 'metric' then metrics.direct_parent_id
            when all_graph_resources.resource_type in ('model', 'snapshot', 'test') then models.direct_parent_id
            else null
        end as direct_parent_id,
        case when all_graph_resources.resource_type = 'test' and models.is_primary_relationship = cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }}) then cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }}) else cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }}) end as is_primary_test_relationship
    from all_graph_resources
    left join direct_model_relationships as models
        on all_graph_resources.resource_id = models.resource_id
    left join direct_exposure_relationships as exposures
        on all_graph_resources.resource_id = exposures.resource_id
    left join direct_metrics_relationships as metrics
        on all_graph_resources.resource_id = metrics.resource_id
),

final as (
    select
        {{ dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key(['resource_id', 'direct_parent_id']) }} as unique_id,
        *
    from direct_relationships
)

select * from final

model.dbt_project_evaluator.int_model_te.name: int_model_test_summary
model.dbt_project_evaluator.int_model_te.raw_code:
with 

all_graph_resources as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_all_graph_resources') }}
    where is_excluded = cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
),

relationships as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_direct_relationships') }}
),

count_column_tests as (
    
    select 
        relationships.direct_parent_id, 
        all_graph_resources.column_name,
        sum(case
                when all_graph_resources.is_test_unique = cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
                then 1
                else 0
            end
         ) as test_unique_count,
        {%- for test_set in var('primary_key_test_macros') %}
            {%- set outer_loop = loop -%}
        count(distinct case when
                {%- for test in test_set %}
                all_graph_resources.is_{{ test.split('.')[1] }} = cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }}) {%- if not loop.last %} or {% endif %}
                {%- endfor %}
            then relationships.resource_id else null end
        ) as primary_key_method_{{ outer_loop.index }}_count,
        {%- endfor %}
        count(distinct relationships.resource_id) as tests_count
    from all_graph_resources
    left join relationships
        on all_graph_resources.resource_id = relationships.resource_id
    where all_graph_resources.resource_type = 'test'
    and relationships.is_primary_test_relationship = cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
    group by relationships.direct_parent_id, all_graph_resources.column_name
),

count_column_constraints as (

    select
        node_unique_id as direct_parent_id,
        name as column_name,
        case
            when has_not_null_constraint = cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})
            then 1
            else 0
        end as constraint_not_null_count,
        constraints_count
    from {{ ref('base_node_columns') }}

),

combine_column_counts as (

    select
        count_column_tests.*,
        count_column_tests.test_unique_count + count_column_constraints.constraint_not_null_count as primary_key_mixed_method_count,
        count_column_constraints.constraints_count
    from count_column_tests
    left join count_column_constraints
        on count_column_tests.direct_parent_id = count_column_constraints.direct_parent_id
        and count_column_tests.column_name = count_column_constraints.column_name

),

agg_test_relationships as (

    select 
        direct_parent_id, 
        case when cast(sum(case
                when (
                    {%- for test_set in var('primary_key_test_macros') %}
                        {%- set compare_value = test_set | length %}
                    primary_key_method_{{ loop.index }}_count >= {{ compare_value}}
                        or
                    {%- endfor %}
                    primary_key_mixed_method_count >= 2
                ) then 1
                else 0
            end
        ) as {{ dbt.type_int() }}) >= 1 then cast(1 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }}) else cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }}) end as is_primary_key_tested,
        cast(sum(tests_count) as {{ dbt.type_int()}}) as number_of_tests_on_model,
        cast(sum(constraints_count) as {{ dbt.type_int()}}) as number_of_constraints_on_model
    from combine_column_counts
    group by direct_parent_id

),

final as (
    select 
        all_graph_resources.resource_name,
        all_graph_resources.resource_type,
        all_graph_resources.model_type,
        cast(coalesce(agg_test_relationships.is_primary_key_tested, cast(0 as {{ dbt.type_boolean() }})) as {{ dbt.type_boolean()}}) as is_primary_key_tested,
        cast(coalesce(agg_test_relationships.number_of_tests_on_model, 0) as {{ dbt.type_int()}}) as number_of_tests_on_model,
        cast(coalesce(agg_test_relationships.number_of_constraints_on_model, 0) as {{ dbt.type_int()}}) as number_of_constraints_on_model
    from all_graph_resources
    left join agg_test_relationships
        on all_graph_resources.resource_id = agg_test_relationships.direct_parent_id
    where
        all_graph_resources.resource_type in ('model', 'seed', 'source', 'snapshot')
)

# Model: snapshot_salesforce_cost_center

## Business Purpose
This snapshot tracks changes to Salesforce cost centre code records over time so downstream raw DV processing can consume a stable, historized source.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Sources from `stg_salesforce__cost_center_codes`.
- Uses `salesforce_cost_centre_id` as the snapshot unique key.
- Uses `timestamp` strategy with `last_modified_date` to track payload changes. Salesforce automatically updates this timestamp whenever any cost centre attribute changes.

## Sources & Dependencies
- Source model: `stg_salesforce__cost_center_codes`.
- Consumed by `int_dv_salesforce_cost_center` in the raw Data Vault cost centre lineage.

## Key Fields
- `cost_center_bk`
- `salesforce_cost_centre_id`
- `cost_center_name`
- `business_unit`
- `commercial_entity`
- `contracting_entity`
- `last_modified_date`
- `record_source`
- `load_date_time`

## Update Frequency
- Updated whenever dbt snapshots are run and source values differ from prior captured state.

## Testing Note
- Uniqueness is tested only on current rows (`dbt_valid_to is null`) rather than the full historized snapshot.
- This keeps the uniqueness assertion focused on active records and avoids an unnecessary full table scan across snapshot history.

- Sources from `stg_salesforce__opportunity`.

## Testing Note

snapshot.cr_project.snapshot_standard_co.name: snapshot_standard_cost_rate
snapshot.cr_project.snapshot_standard_co.description:
# Model: snapshot_standard_cost_rate

## Business Purpose
This snapshot tracks changes to the standard cost rate for project roles in Workday over time. It enables historical analysis and auditing of cost rate changes for project roles.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Captures all records from the staging model `stg_workday__standard_cost_rate`.
- `standard_cost_rate_bk` (a composite key of Project_Role_ID, Effective_From, and Currency) is used as the unique key.
- Follows a timestamp strategy to record changes whenever the effective date or other tracked fields are updated.

## Sources & Dependencies
- Source: `stg_workday__standard_cost_rate` (staging model for Workday standard cost rate data)
- Depends on the external Workday data source and the staging transformation logic.

## Key Fields
- `Project_Role_ID`: Unique identifier for the project role.
- `Effective_From`: Date when the cost rate became effective.
- `Project_Role`: Name of the project role.
- `Standard_Cost_Rate`: Standard cost rate for the project role.
- `record_source`: Source file for the record.
- `load_date_time`: Timestamp when the record was loaded.

## Update Frequency
- Updated whenever the source data in Workday changes and the dbt snapshot is run (typically daily or as scheduled).

## Additional Notes
- Ensures historical tracking of cost rate changes for compliance and reporting.
- Follows dbt and project style guide conventions for naming, structure, and documentation.

snapshot.cr_project.snapshot_time_sheet.name: snapshot_time_sheet
snapshot.cr_project.snapshot_time_sheet.description:
## Overview

The `time_sheet` snapshot tracks historical changes to timesheet records sourced from the `stg_workday_time_block_audit` model. This snapshot enables auditing and analysis of timesheet data over time, capturing every change to key business attributes.

For reporting purposes, this snapshot also joins and includes the IDs for project role and practice, as these are not present in the original source but are required for downstream analytics and business consumption.

## Purpose

- Maintain a full history of timesheet records for compliance and auditability.
- Detect and record changes to important timesheet fields, such as hours worked, billing rates, and statuses.
- Support reporting on both current and historical states of timesheet data.

## Change Detection Strategy
This snapshot uses the **check strategy** with a set of business-critical columns. A new record is created whenever any of these columns change for a given timesheet key (`TIMESHEET_BK`). 
The snapshot records the validity period for each version using `dbt_valid_from` and `dbt_valid_to` fields.
The snaphost use 'hard_deleted = `ignore` because the Time_Block_Audit report is using high water mark and it also uses is_deleted field to identify deletion.

### Tracked Columns

- `TASK_CODE`
- `TOTAL_HOURS__TIME_TRACKING`
- `BILLABLE_HOURS`
- `BILLING_CURRENCY`
- `BILLABLE_RATE`
- `BILLING_STATUS`
- `REVENUE_STATUS`
- `INVOICE_NUMBER`
- `OVERRIDE_RATE`
- `CALCULATED_DATE`
- `IS_DELETED`

## Additional Notes

- The snapshot is refreshed as part of the dbt run process.
- Ensure that the source staging model (`stg_workday_time_block_audit`) is up to date for accurate snapshotting.
- For more information, refer to the [dbt snapshot documentation](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/snapshots).

{{
  config(
    target_schema='snapshots',
    unique_key='timesheet_bk',
    strategy='check',
    check_cols=['task_code', 'timesheet_status', 'total_hours__time_tracking', 'billable_hours', 'billable_rate', 'billing_currency', 'billing_status', 'revenue_status',
                'invoice_number', 'override_rate', 'calculated_Date', 'is_deleted'],
    hard_deletes = 'ignore'
  )
}}

with 
	practice as (
	    select

         left join  
          practice
            on time_block_audit.Practice = practice.Practice_Name
         left join 
          project_role
            on time_block_audit.Project_Role = project_role.Project_Role )

select 
* 
from final

snapshot.cr_project.snapshot_workday_wor.description: Snapshot of Workday worker records using check strategy. Tracks all column-level changes over time. Includes derived effective_termination_date and effective_recent_termination_date columns that map termination dates which predate hire_date — an onboarding artefact for employees migrated from Telstra Purple.

termination_date.name: termination_date
termination_date.description: Raw termination date as received from Workday. May predate hire_date for Purple migrants.

recent_termination_date.name: recent_termination_date
recent_termination_date.description: Raw most recent approved termination date from Workday. May predate hire_date for Purple migrants.

supervisory_organisation_hierarchy.name: supervisory_organisation_hierarchy
supervisory_organisation_hierarchy.description: Raw supervisory organisation hierarchy string from Workday (delimiter ' > ').

effective_termination_date.name: effective_termination_date
effective_termination_date.description: Derived termination date. Set to var('high_date') when termination_date < hire_date (Purple onboarding artefact), otherwise equal to termination_date. Use this column in downstream models.

effective_recent_termination_date.name: effective_recent_termination_date
effective_recent_termination_date.description: Derived most recent approved termination date. Set to var('high_date') when recent_termination_date < hire_date (Purple onboarding artefact), otherwise equal to recent_termination_date. Use this column in downstream models.

snapshot.cr_project.snapshot_workday_wor.raw_code:
{{
    config(
        target_schema='snapshots',
        unique_key='employee_bk',
        strategy='check',
        check_cols='all',
        hard_deletes='ignore'
    )
}}

select
    employee_bk,
    first_name,
    last_name,
    work_email,
    worker_type,
    worker_subtype,
    region_id,
    hire_date,
    cost_center_id,
    function,
    practice,
    working_hours,
    location,
    location_hierarchies,
    fte,
    scheduled_weekly_hours,
    default_weekly_hours,
    termination_date,
    business_title,
    job_profile,
    supervisory_organisation_hierarchy,
    recent_termination_date,
    has_future_termination_event,
    record_source,
    termination_date                                                     AS original_termination_date,
    recent_termination_date                                              AS original_recent_termination_date,
    -- Employees migrated from Telstra Purple are onboarded into Versent Workday with a
    -- historical termination date prior to their Versent hire_date. This is an onboarding
    -- artefact and should not be treated as an active termination. The derived columns
    -- below map those dates to high_date so downstream filters can treat them as open-ended.
    IFF(termination_date IS NULL OR termination_date < hire_date, TO_DATE('{{ var("high_date") }}'), termination_date)               AS effective_termination_date,
    IFF(recent_termination_date IS NOT NULL AND recent_termination_date < hire_date, TO_DATE('{{ var("high_date") }}'), recent_termination_date) AS effective_recent_termination_date
from {{ ref('stg_workday_workers') }}

test.cr_project.dbt_utils_mutually_exclu.name: dbt_utils_mutually_exclusive_ranges_dvbridge_booking_effective_from__resource_forecast_sid__effective_to
test.cr_project.dbt_utils_mutually_exclu.compiled_code:
with window_functions as (

    select
        
        resource_forecast_sid as partition_by_col,
        
        effective_from as lower_bound,
        effective_to as upper_bound,

        lead(effective_from) over (
            partition by resource_forecast_sid
            order by effective_from, effective_to
        ) as next_lower_bound,

        row_number() over (
            partition by resource_forecast_sid
            order by effective_from desc, effective_to desc
        ) = 1 as is_last_record

    from datavault__business.dvbridge_booking

),

calc as (
    -- We want to return records where one of our assumptions fails, so we'll use
    -- the `not` function with `and` statements so we can write our assumptions more cleanly
    select
        *,

        -- For each record: lower_bound should be < upper_bound.
        -- Coalesce it to return an error on the null case (implicit assumption
        -- these columns are not_null)
        coalesce(
            lower_bound < upper_bound,
            false
        ) as lower_bound_less_than_upper_bound,

        -- For each record: upper_bound <= the next lower_bound.
        -- Coalesce it to handle null cases for the last record.
        coalesce(
            upper_bound <= next_lower_bound,
            is_last_record,
            false
        ) as upper_bound_less_than_or_equal_to_next_lower_bound

    from window_functions

),

validation_errors as (

    select
        *
    from calc

    where not(
        -- THE FOLLOWING SHOULD BE TRUE --
        lower_bound_less_than_upper_bound
        and upper_bound_less_than_or_equal_to_next_lower_bound
    )
)

select * from validation_errors

test.cr_project.fact_forecast_booking_am.raw_code:
{% docs fact_forecast_booking_amount_not_zero_when_upstream_non_zero_parametrized %}

Warn when a selected project-month has non-zero forecast potential upstream in TM logic,
but produces zero amount in TM branch output.

Vars:
- ffb_amount_project_bk (default PROJ-035856)
- ffb_amount_month_start (default 2026-05-01)

{% enddocs %}
{{ config(
    severity = 'warn',
    tags = ['booking_forecast']
    )
}}

{% set project_bk = var('ffb_amount_project_bk', 'PROJ-035856') %}
{% set month_start = var('ffb_amount_month_start', '2026-05-01') %}

with upstream as (
    select
        resource_forecast_sid,
        project_bk,
        date_bk,
        forecasted_hours,
        contract_billing_rate,
        working_hours,
        contract_is_rate_daily,
        case
            when contract_is_rate_daily then contract_billing_rate / nullif(working_hours, 0)
            else contract_billing_rate
        end as expected_hourly_rate
    from {{ ref('int__booking_forecast') }}
    where project_bk = '{{ project_bk }}'
      and primary_project_hierarchy in ('Prof Serve: TM', 'VMS: TM')
      and revenue_type = 'FORECAST'
      and to_date(date_bk) between to_date('{{ month_start }}') and last_day(to_date('{{ month_start }}'))
),
expected_non_zero as (
    select
        resource_forecast_sid,
        project_bk,
        date_bk,
        forecasted_hours,
        contract_billing_rate,
        working_hours,
        contract_is_rate_daily,
        expected_hourly_rate,
        forecasted_hours * expected_hourly_rate as expected_amount
    from upstream
    where coalesce(forecasted_hours, 0) > 0
      and coalesce(expected_hourly_rate, 0) > 0
),
tm_output as (
    select
        resource_forecast_sid,
        project_bk,
        date_bk,
        amount
    from {{ ref('int__booking_forecast__time_and_materials__all_stages') }}
    where project_bk = '{{ project_bk }}'
      and to_date(date_bk) between to_date('{{ month_start }}') and last_day(to_date('{{ month_start }}'))
)
select
    e.project_bk,
    e.date_bk,
    e.resource_forecast_sid,
    e.forecasted_hours,
    e.contract_billing_rate,
    e.working_hours,
    e.contract_is_rate_daily,
    e.expected_hourly_rate,
    e.expected_amount,
    t.amount as actual_amount
from expected_non_zero e
left join tm_output t
    on e.resource_forecast_sid = t.resource_forecast_sid
where coalesce(t.amount, 0) = 0

with 
    opportunity as (
        select 
            opportunity_bk,
            dim_opportunity_sid,
            deal_value
        from 
            data_mart.dim_opportunity
    ),
    daily_amount as (
        select 
            dim_opportunity_sid,
            sum(daily_amount) as sum_daily_amount
        from
            data_mart.fact_sow_amount
        WHERE
			effective_to = '2900-12-30 23:59:59.000'
        group by
            dim_opportunity_sid
    ),
    sow_values as (
        select
            opportunity.opportunity_bk,
            opportunity.dim_opportunity_sid,
            opportunity.deal_value,
            daily_amount.sum_daily_amount,
            abs(opportunity.deal_value - daily_amount.sum_daily_amount) as diff
        from
            opportunity
            join
                daily_amount
                on 
                    opportunity.dim_opportunity_sid = daily_amount.dim_opportunity_sid
    ),
    errors as (
        SELECT
            opportunity_bk,
            deal_value,
            sum_daily_amount,
            diff
        FROM 
            sow_values
        WHERE diff > 5
    )
SELECT 
    *
FROM 
    errors

test.cr_project.int__booking_forecast__f.raw_code:
{% docs test_stg_booking_forecast_fixed_price_sow_check %}

Tests that, for Fixed Price Projects, Forecasted Revenue only uses the 'Remaining Revenue', i.e.
  SOW - FInalized Actuals = Remaining Amount

Multiple derivation tables collect Actual Revenue, Sow Amount, Forecasted Hours and a Ramaining Dollar amount for Fixed Price Projects.
This test makes sure that:
  [Forecast Amounts in int_booking_forecast_fixed_price] + [Finalized Actuals] = [SOW Amount]

This test is also done in rep_revenue_forecast_fixed_price_sow_check downstream
{% enddocs %}
{{ config(
    severity = 'warn',
    tags = ['booking_forecast']
    ) }}

with 
  actuals as (
    select
      project_bk,
      min(opportunity_project_value) as opportunity_project_value,
      round(sum(month_revenue_amount), 2) as actual_amount
    from {{ ref('int__project_revenue__calendar') }}
    group by project_bk
  ),
  forecast as (
    select
      project_bk,
      round(sum(amount), 2) as forecast_amount
    from
      {{ ref('int__booking_forecast__fixed_price') }}
    group by project_bk
  )
select
    forecast.PROJECT_BK,
    actual_amount,
    forecast_amount,
    opportunity_project_value,
    actual_amount + forecast_amount as total_amount,
    total_amount - opportunity_project_value as sow_difference
from forecast
left join actuals
    on actuals.project_bk = forecast.project_bk
where sow_difference is null or abs(sow_difference) > 5

test.cr_project.int__opportunity_field_h.name: int__opportunity_field_history_pivot__amount_belongs_to_opportunity
test.cr_project.int__opportunity_field_h.raw_code:
{% docs test_opportunity_field_history_pivot_amount_belongs_to_opportunity %}

Tests that forward-filled values in int_fact_opportunity_field_history__pivot
belong to the same opportunity. If the LAST_VALUE window functions are missing
PARTITION BY OPPORTUNITY_BK, values from one opportunity bleed into another.

This test finds rows where the forward-filled amount does not match any Amount
value ever recorded for that opportunity in the source history.
A non-empty result means cross-opportunity data leakage.

{% enddocs %}
{{ config(
    severity = 'error',
    tags = ['opportunity_field_history']
) }}

with pivot_result as (
    select
        opportunity_bk,
        amount
    from {{ ref('int_fact_opportunity_field_history__pivot') }}
    where amount is not null
),

valid_amounts as (
    select distinct
        b.opportunity_bk,
        bc.new_value as amount
    from {{ ref('dvbridge_opportunity_field_history') }} b
    join {{ ref('bc_opportunity_field_history') }} bc
        on b.h_opportunity_field_history_sid = bc.h_opportunity_field_history_sid
    where bc.field = 'Amount'
      and bc.new_value is not null
)

select
    p.opportunity_bk,
    p.amount
from pivot_result p
left join valid_amounts v
    on p.opportunity_bk = v.opportunity_bk
    and p.amount = v.amount
where v.amount is null

test.cr_project.rep_revenue_forecast_dea.name: rep_revenue_forecast_deal_value_check_fixed_price
test.cr_project.rep_revenue_forecast_dea.compiled_code:
SELECT
  REP_REVENUE.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID,
  MAX(bridge_opportunity_project.OPPORTUNITY_BK) as OPPORTUNITY_BK,
  MAX(bridge_opportunity_project.project_bk) as project_bk,
  MAX(bridge_opportunity_project.Primary_Project_Hierarchy) as Primary_Project_Hierarchy,
  SUM(REP_REVENUE.AMOUNT) as revenue_amount,
  MIN(bridge_opportunity_project.opportunity_project_value) as value,
  revenue_amount - value as difference
FROM reporting.rep_revenue  
LEFT JOIN data_mart.bridge_opportunity_project
    ON REP_REVENUE.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID = bridge_opportunity_project.H_OPPORTUNITY_SID
LEFT JOIN data_mart.dim_stage
    ON REP_REVENUE.DIM_STAGE_SID = dim_stage.DIM_STAGE_SID
WHERE 1=1
  -- Create PIT for current view of world as this is the only timeframe we can affect
  AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() BETWEEN REP_REVENUE.EFFECTIVE_FROM AND REP_REVENUE.EFFECTIVE_TO
  
  -- Filter on projects with a hierarchy and filter out Stax/Ping opportunities
  AND bridge_opportunity_project.PRIMARY_PROJECT_HIERARCHY IS NOT NULL
  
  AND DIM_STAGE.stage_bk = 'CLOSED_WON'

  AND bridge_opportunity_project.PRIMARY_PROJECT_HIERARCHY = 'Prof Serve: FP'
GROUP BY REP_REVENUE.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
-- Filter our rounding errors
HAVING ABS(difference) > 10
ORDER BY ABS(difference) desc

test.cr_project.sat_project_int_dv_proje.name: sat_project_int_dv_project_latest_workday_sat_project_workday_
test.cr_project.sat_project_int_dv_proje.compiled_code:
with sat_ranked as (
    select
        h_project_sid,
        project_owner,
        load_date_time,
        row_number() over (
            partition by h_project_sid
            order by load_date_time desc
        ) as rn
    from datavault__raw.sat_project_workday
),
sat_latest as (
    select
        h_project_sid,
        project_owner
    from sat_ranked
    where rn = 1
),

int_proj as (
    select
        h_project_sid,
        project_owner
    from datavault__raw_int.int_dv_project_workday
),
joined as (
    select
        coalesce(s.h_project_sid, i.h_project_sid) as h_project_sid,
        s.project_owner as sat_project_owner,
        i.project_owner as int_project_owner
    from sat_latest s
    inner join int_proj i on s.h_project_sid = i.h_project_sid)

select *
from joined
where sat_project_owner != int_project_owner

-- Fails if adjusted model still contains overlapping effective periods
-- for same project_bk + employee_bk + project_role_bk
-- Ensures no overlapping date ranges exist after adjustment logic

with ordered as (

    select
        project_cost_rate_bk,
        project_bk,
        employee_bk,
        project_role_bk,
        start_date,
        end_date,

        lag(end_date) over (
            partition by project_bk, employee_bk, project_role_bk
            order by start_date, end_date
        ) as prev_end_date

    from datavault__business.bc_project_cost_rate
)

select *
from ordered
where prev_end_date is not null
  and start_date <= prev_end_date

with salesforce_cost_centers as (
    select
        distinct
        upper(region_bk) as region,
        upper(business_unit) as business_unit,
        upper(practice_bk) as practice, 
        cost_center_code__c
    from landing_salesforce.stg_salesforce__opportunity
    where region_bk is not null
      and business_unit is not null
      and practice_bk is not null
),

mapped_cost_centers as (
    select
        distinct
        upper(region) as region,
        upper(business_unit) as business_unit,
        upper(practice) as practice
    from staging.stg_seeds__salesforce_workday_mappings
)

select
    s.*
from salesforce_cost_centers s
left join mapped_cost_centers m
    on s.region = m.region
    and s.business_unit = m.business_unit
    and s.practice = m.practice
where m.region is null and s.cost_center_code__c is null

macro.cr_project.copy_into.description:
# Macro: copy_into

## Business Purpose
Main entry point for loading raw JSON files from a Snowflake external stage into a landing table. Orchestrates table creation, optional truncation, and the COPY INTO operation in a single call.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Reads `DBT_LANDING_DB` from environment variables to determine the target database.
- Derives the target schema as `LANDING_<source_name>` and the target table as `CI_<api>`.
- Creates the target landing table if it does not already exist (via `copy_into_create_target_table`).
- Optionally truncates the target table before loading when `truncate=true`.
- Resolves the file pattern as `<source_name>/<api>/.*<api>.*[.]json`.
- Executes the COPY INTO statement at runtime; returns the generated SQL otherwise.

## Arguments
| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_name` | string | required | Source system identifier (e.g. `workday`). Used to derive schema name and file path. |
| `api` | string | required | API / endpoint name (e.g. `workers`). Used to derive table name and file pattern. |
| `file_format` | string | required | Fully-qualified Snowflake file format name to use for parsing. |
| `on_error` | string | `'CONTINUE'` | Snowflake `ON_ERROR` behaviour (`CONTINUE`, `SKIP_FILE`, `ABORT_STATEMENT`). |
| `force` | boolean | `false` | When `true`, re-loads files already loaded (Snowflake `FORCE = true`). |
| `truncate` | boolean | `false` | When `true`, truncates the target table before loading. |

## Example Usage
Within a model's `pre_hook`, invoke the macro to load staged JSON files into a landing table before processing:

```jinja

arguments.name: source_name
arguments.description: Source system identifier (e.g. `workday`). Used to derive the landing schema name and the file-path pattern.

arguments.name: api
arguments.description: API / endpoint name (e.g. `workers`). Used to derive the landing table name and the file-path pattern.

arguments.name: file_format
arguments.description: Fully-qualified Snowflake file format name used to parse staged files.

arguments.name: on_error
arguments.description: Snowflake ON_ERROR behaviour. Defaults to `CONTINUE`.

arguments.name: force
arguments.description: When true, re-loads files already recorded in the load history. Defaults to false.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.description: When true, truncates the target table before loading. Defaults to false.

# Macro: copy_into_create_target_table

## Business Purpose
Executes a `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` for the target landing table at runtime. Returns `select 1` after execution so it can be safely called in a dbt context.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- The landing table schema is `(raw_data VARIANT, filename STRING, file_row_number NUMBER, loaded_at TIMESTAMP_NTZ DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())`.
- Only executes when dbt is in execute mode; returns the generated SQL otherwise.

## Arguments
| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `landing_db` | string | Target Snowflake database. |
| `source_name` | string | Source system identifier. |
| `api` | string | API / endpoint name. |

# Macro: copy_into_from_vars

## Business Purpose
Convenience wrapper around `copy_into` that reads all arguments from dbt variables, enabling the macro to be driven entirely from the `--vars` flag without writing Jinja.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Reads `source_name`, `api`, `copy_into_file_format`, `copy_into_on_error`, `copy_into_force`, and `copy_into_truncate` from dbt vars.
- Defaults: `on_error='CONTINUE'`, `force=false`, `truncate=true`.
- Delegates to `copy_into` with the resolved values.

## Arguments
None — all arguments are supplied via dbt `--vars`.

| Variable | dbt var key | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Source system | `source_name` | required |
| API / endpoint | `api` | required |
| File format | `copy_into_file_format` | required |
| On error behaviour | `copy_into_on_error` | `CONTINUE` |
| Force reload | `copy_into_force` | `false` |
| Truncate before load | `copy_into_truncate` | `true` |

## Additional Notes
- Example: `dbt run-operation copy_into_from_vars --vars '{source_name: workday, api: workers, copy_into_file_format: RAW_DB.LANDING_WORKDAY.WORKDAY_JSON_FORMAT}'`

macro.cr_project.copy_into_sql.name: copy_into_sql
macro.cr_project.copy_into_sql.description:
# Macro: copy_into_sql

## Business Purpose
Generates the Snowflake `COPY INTO` SQL statement for loading raw JSON files from an external stage into a landing table. Returns the SQL string without executing it.

## Business Logic & Key Calculations
- Reads `DBT_LANDING_DB` from environment variables.
- Derives the target relation using `copy_into_target_relation`.
- Resolves the source stage (defaults to `copy_into_source_stage` result) and file pattern (defaults to `copy_into_pattern` result) when not explicitly provided.
- Selects `$1` as `raw_data` (VARIANT), `METADATA$FILENAME` as `filename`, and `METADATA$FILE_ROW_NUMBER` as `file_row_number`.

## Arguments
| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_name` | string | required | Source system identifier. |
| `api` | string | required | API / endpoint name. |
| `source_stage` | string | `none` | Override the source stage path. Defaults to the derived stage. |
| `file_format` | string | required | Fully-qualified Snowflake file format name. |
| `pattern` | string | `none` | Override the file regex pattern. Defaults to the derived pattern. |
| `on_error` | string | `'CONTINUE'` | Snowflake `ON_ERROR` value. |
| `force` | boolean | `false` | Snowflake `FORCE` flag. |
| `truncate` | boolean | `false` | Unused in SQL generation; kept for interface parity. |

macro.cr_project.generate_forecast_query.name: generate_forecast_query
macro.cr_project.generate_forecast_query.macro_sql:
{% macro generate_forecast_query(forecast_external_table) %}

{%- set month_columns = get_month_column_list() -%}

    WITH base as (
        SELECT
            value,
            METADATA$FILENAME                                                             AS record_source,
            REGEXP_SUBSTR(METADATA$FILENAME, '\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}_\\d{2}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}') AS load_date_str,
            TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ(load_date_str, 'YYYY-MM-DD_HH24-MI-SS') AS file_timestamp
        FROM {{ ref(forecast_external_table) }} 
    ),  
    pivot as (
    SELECT
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c1::STRING)),''),'-')   AS type,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c2::STRING)),''),'-')   AS old_region,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c3::STRING)),''),'-')   AS region,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c4::STRING)),''),'-')   AS cost_center_code, 
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c5::STRING)),''),'-')   AS cost_center,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c6::STRING)),''),'-')   AS business_unit,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c7::STRING)),''),'-')   AS revenue_category_id,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c8::STRING)),''),'-')   AS revenue_group,
        {% for columns in month_columns %}
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(VALUE:c{{loop.index + 8}}::string),''),'-') AS "{{columns}}",
        {% endfor %}
        record_source,
        file_timestamp
    FROM base
    ),
    unpivoted as (
    SELECT
        *
    FROM pivot
        unpivot(
        revenue for month in ({{ '"' ~ month_columns | join('","') ~ '"' }})
        )
    ),
    target_forecast AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Jan' THEN 1
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Feb' THEN 2
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Mar' THEN 3
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Apr' THEN 4
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'May' THEN 5
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Jun' THEN 6
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Jul' THEN 7
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Aug' THEN 8
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Sep' THEN 9
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Oct' THEN 10
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Nov' THEN 11
            WHEN substring(unpivoted.month,1,3) = 'Dec' THEN 12
        END AS Month_Num,
        20 || right(month,2) AS YEAR,
        unpivoted.old_region,
        unpivoted.region,
        unpivoted.cost_center_code,
        unpivoted.cost_center,
        unpivoted.business_unit,
        unpivoted.revenue_category_id,
        unpivoted.revenue_group,
        TRY_TO_NUMBER(regexp_replace(unpivoted.revenue,',')) AS revenue,
        RECORD_SOURCE,
        file_timestamp
    FROM
        unpivoted
    )
    SELECT
        *
    FROM
        target_forecast


{% endmacro %}

macro.cr_project.generate_forecast_query.name: generate_forecast_query_after_fy2026
macro.cr_project.generate_forecast_query.macro_sql:
{% macro generate_forecast_query_after_fy2026(forecast_external_table) %}

{%- set month_columns = get_fy_months() -%}

    WITH base as (
        SELECT
            value,
            METADATA$FILENAME                                                             AS record_source,
            REGEXP_SUBSTR(METADATA$FILENAME, '\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}_\\d{2}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}') AS load_date_str,
            TO_TIMESTAMP_TZ(load_date_str, 'YYYY-MM-DD_HH24-MI-SS') AS file_timestamp,
            REGEXP_SUBSTR(METADATA$FILENAME, 'fy\\d{4}') AS fy_string,
            TO_NUMBER(SUBSTR(fy_string, 3, 4)) AS base_year
        FROM {{ ref(forecast_external_table) }} 
    ),  
    pivot as (
    SELECT
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c1::STRING)),''),'-')   AS type,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c2::STRING)),''),'-')   AS region,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c3::STRING)),''),'-')   AS cost_center_code,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c4::STRING)),''),'-')   AS cost_center, 
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c5::STRING)),''),'-')   AS business_unit,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c6::STRING)),''),'-')   AS revenue_category_id,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c7::STRING)),''),'-')   AS revenue_group,
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(VALUE:c8::STRING)),''),'-')   AS practice,
        {% for columns in month_columns %}
        NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(VALUE:c{{loop.index + 8}}::string),''),'-') AS "{{columns}}",
        {% endfor %}
        base_year,
        record_source,
        file_timestamp
    FROM base
    ),
    unpivoted as (
    SELECT
        *
    FROM pivot
        unpivot(
        revenue for month in ({{ '"' ~ month_columns | join('","') ~ '"' }})
        )
    ),
    target_forecast AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN month = 'Jan' THEN 1
            WHEN month = 'Feb' THEN 2
            WHEN month = 'Mar' THEN 3
            WHEN month = 'Apr' THEN 4
            WHEN month = 'May' THEN 5
            WHEN month = 'Jun' THEN 6
            WHEN month = 'Jul' THEN 7
            WHEN month = 'Aug' THEN 8
            WHEN month = 'Sep' THEN 9
            WHEN month = 'Oct' THEN 10
            WHEN month = 'Nov' THEN 11
            WHEN month = 'Dec' THEN 12
        END AS Month_Num,
        CASE
            WHEN month IN ('Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun') THEN base_year + 1
            ELSE base_year
        END as year,
        unpivoted.region,
        unpivoted.cost_center_code,
        unpivoted.cost_center,
        unpivoted.business_unit,
        unpivoted.revenue_category_id,
        unpivoted.revenue_group,
        unpivoted.practice,
        TRY_TO_NUMBER(REGEXP_REPLACE(revenue, ',')) AS revenue,
        RECORD_SOURCE,
        file_timestamp
    FROM
        unpivoted
    )
    SELECT
        *
    FROM
        target_forecast


{% endmacro %}

macro.cr_project.rep_revenue_forecast_de.macro_sql:
{% macro rep_revenue_forecast_deal_value_test(PRIMARY_PROJECT_HIERARCHY) %}
SELECT
  REP_REVENUE.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID,
  MAX(bridge_opportunity_project.OPPORTUNITY_BK) as OPPORTUNITY_BK,
  MAX(bridge_opportunity_project.project_bk) as project_bk,
  MAX(bridge_opportunity_project.Primary_Project_Hierarchy) as Primary_Project_Hierarchy,
  SUM(REP_REVENUE.AMOUNT) as revenue_amount,
  MIN(bridge_opportunity_project.opportunity_project_value) as value,
  revenue_amount - value as difference
FROM {{ ref('rep_revenue') }}  
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('bridge_opportunity_project') }}
    ON REP_REVENUE.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID = bridge_opportunity_project.H_OPPORTUNITY_SID
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('dim_stage') }}
    ON REP_REVENUE.DIM_STAGE_SID = dim_stage.DIM_STAGE_SID
WHERE 1=1
  -- Create PIT for current view of world as this is the only timeframe we can affect
  AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() BETWEEN REP_REVENUE.EFFECTIVE_FROM AND REP_REVENUE.EFFECTIVE_TO
  
  -- Filter on projects with a hierarchy and filter out Stax/Ping opportunities
  AND bridge_opportunity_project.PRIMARY_PROJECT_HIERARCHY IS NOT NULL
  
  AND DIM_STAGE.stage_bk = 'CLOSED_WON'

  AND bridge_opportunity_project.PRIMARY_PROJECT_HIERARCHY = '{{PRIMARY_PROJECT_HIERARCHY}}'
GROUP BY REP_REVENUE.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
-- Filter our rounding errors
HAVING ABS(difference) > 10
ORDER BY ABS(difference) desc

{% endmacro %}

macro.cr_project.sv_yaml_forecasting.macro_sql:
{% macro sv_yaml_forecasting() %}
{% set yaml_content %}
name: forecasting
description: >
  Forward-looking resource forecasting -- forecasted hours, FTE, weighted FTE, billing rate
  and forecast amount per employee x project x opportunity x date. Sourced from
  FACT_FORECAST_BOOKING. Use this view for resource-planning questions, FTE pipelines and
  forecast vs actuals comparisons.

module_custom_instructions:
  sql_generation: |
    - DEDUP REQUIRED. fact_forecast_booking carries multiple revisions per (employee, date,
      opportunity) keyed by EFFECTIVE_FROM. Without deduplication, SUM aggregates double-count.
      Always wrap aggregations in a CTE that keeps only the latest revision:

        WITH dedup AS (
          SELECT *
          FROM __fact_forecast_booking
          QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID, DIM_DATE_SID, DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
            ORDER BY EFFECTIVE_FROM DESC
          ) = 1
        )
        SELECT ... FROM dedup ...

    - "Weighted FTE" = FTE x probability of close (already pre-computed on the fact table).
      Use weighted_fte for probability-adjusted resource planning; use raw fte for capacity.
    - dim_opportunity.is_closed is VARIANT-typed. Filter using TRY_CAST(is_closed::STRING AS BOOLEAN)
      or compare against the string 'true'/'false'.
    - When the user asks about "forecast" vs "booked", treat them as synonyms in this domain.
      The PBI distinction (forecast/booked/actuals via TABLE_SOURCE) only applies to the
      revenue_pipeline semantic view.
    - Format dollar amounts with TO_VARCHAR(value, '$999,999,999.00').

tables:

  - name: dim_date
    description: Calendar and fiscal-year date dimension.
    base_table:
      database: __TARGET_DATABASE__
      schema: DATA_MART
      table: DIM_DATE
    primary_key:
      columns:
        - DIM_DATE_SID
    dimensions:
      - name: dim_date_sid
        expr: DIM_DATE_SID
        data_type: BINARY
        access_modifier: private_access
      - name: month_name_short_year
        expr: MONTH_NAME_SHORT_YEAR
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: year_number
        expr: YEAR_NUMBER
        data_type: NUMBER
      - name: fy_number_string
        expr: FY_NUMBER_STRING
        data_type: TEXT
        synonyms: [fiscal year]
      - name: fy_quarter_number_string
        expr: FY_QUARTER_NUMBER_STRING
        data_type: TEXT
    time_dimensions:
      - name: date
        expr: DATE
        data_type: DATE
      - name: month_start_date
        expr: MONTH_START_DATE
        data_type: DATE
      - name: quarter_start_date
        expr: QUARTER_START_DATE
        data_type: DATE
      - name: year_start_date
        expr: YEAR_START_DATE
        data_type: DATE

  - name: dim_employee
    description: Employee master.
    base_table:
      database: __TARGET_DATABASE__
      schema: DATA_MART
      table: DIM_EMPLOYEE
    primary_key:
      columns:
        - DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID
    dimensions:
      - name: dim_employee_sid
        expr: DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID
        data_type: BINARY
        access_modifier: private_access
      - name: full_name
        expr: FIRST_NAME || ' ' || LAST_NAME
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: worker_type
        expr: WORKER_TYPE
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: function
        expr: FUNCTION
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: practice
        expr: PRACTICE
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: location
        expr: LOCATION
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: fte
        expr: FTE
        data_type: NUMBER

  - name: dim_project
    description: Project master.
    base_table:
      database: __TARGET_DATABASE__
      schema: DATA_MART
      table: DIM_PROJECT
    primary_key:
      columns:
        - DIM_PROJECT_SID
    dimensions:
      - name: dim_project_sid
        expr: DIM_PROJECT_SID
        data_type: BINARY
        access_modifier: private_access
      - name: project_name
        expr: PROJECT_NAME
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: project_status
        expr: PROJECT_STATUS
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: service_offering
        expr: SERVICE_OFFERING
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: practice_name
        expr: PRACTICE_NAME
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: project_type
        expr: PROJECT_TYPE
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: client_name
        expr: CLIENT_NAME
        data_type: TEXT

  - name: dim_opportunity
    description: Salesforce opportunity master.
    base_table:
      database: __TARGET_DATABASE__
      schema: DATA_MART
      table: DIM_OPPORTUNITY
    primary_key:
      columns:
        - DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
    dimensions:
      - name: dim_opportunity_sid
        expr: DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
        data_type: BINARY
        access_modifier: private_access
      - name: opportunity_name
        expr: OPPORTUNITY_NAME
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: service_offering
        expr: SERVICE_OFFERING
        data_type: TEXT
      - name: type

        data_type: TEXT
      - name: forecast_category_name

      - name: customer_lead_name

      - name: is_closed
        description: VARIANT in source -- coerced to BOOLEAN here.
        expr: TRY_CAST(IS_CLOSED::STRING AS BOOLEAN)
        data_type: BOOLEAN
      - name: is_won
        expr: IS_WON
        data_type: BOOLEAN
    time_dimensions:

    dimensions:

        data_type: BINARY
        access_modifier: private_access

        expr: COST_CENTER_NAME

  - name: dim_practice
    description: Versent practice.

      database: __TARGET_DATABASE__

    primary_key:

  - name: dim_client
    description: Client master.
    base_table:

    base_table:

        expr: EFFECTIVE_FROM

      - name: effective_to
        expr: EFFECTIVE_TO
        data_type: TIMESTAMP_NTZ

    facts:
      - name: forecasted_hours
        expr: FORECASTED_HOURS
        data_type: NUMBER
      - name: amount

        expr: AMOUNT
        data_type: NUMBER

        expr: SUM(fact_forecast_booking.forecasted_hours)
      - name: total_forecast_amount
        description: Sum of forecast amount. Same dedup caveat as forecasted_hours.
        expr: SUM(fact_forecast_booking.amount)

      - name: total_forecast_fte

        expr: SUM(fact_forecast_booking.fte)
      - name: total_forecast_weighted_fte
        description: Sum of probability-weighted FTE.
        expr: SUM(fact_forecast_booking.weighted_fte)
      - name: avg_contract_billing_rate
        description: Average contract billing rate across forecast bookings.
        expr: AVG(fact_forecast_booking.contract_billing_rate)

verified_queries:

  - name: forecast_hours_by_month_dedup
    question: How many forecasted hours (deduplicated) per month for the next 6 months?
    sql: |
      WITH dedup AS (
        SELECT DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID, DIM_DATE_SID, DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID, FORECASTED_HOURS
        FROM __fact_forecast_booking
        QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
          PARTITION BY DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID, DIM_DATE_SID, DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
          ORDER BY EFFECTIVE_FROM DESC
        ) = 1
      )
      SELECT
        d.MONTH_NAME_SHORT_YEAR  AS month,
        SUM(f.FORECASTED_HOURS)  AS forecasted_hours
      FROM dedup f
      JOIN __dim_date d
        ON f.DIM_DATE_SID = d.DIM_DATE_SID
      WHERE d.DATE BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE() AND DATEADD('MONTH', 6, CURRENT_DATE())
      GROUP BY d.MONTH_NAME_SHORT_YEAR, d.MONTH_START_DATE
      ORDER BY d.MONTH_START_DATE;

  - name: forecast_amount_by_stage_fy26
    question: What is the FY26 forecast amount by pipeline stage?
    sql: |
      WITH dedup AS (
        SELECT DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID, DIM_DATE_SID, DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID, DIM_STAGE_SID, AMOUNT
        FROM __fact_forecast_booking
        QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
          PARTITION BY DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID, DIM_DATE_SID, DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
          ORDER BY EFFECTIVE_FROM DESC
        ) = 1
      )
      SELECT
        s.STAGE_NAME    AS stage,
        SUM(f.AMOUNT)   AS forecast_amount
      FROM dedup f
      JOIN __dim_stage s
        ON f.DIM_STAGE_SID = s.DIM_STAGE_SID
      JOIN __dim_date d
        ON f.DIM_DATE_SID = d.DIM_DATE_SID
      WHERE d.FY_NUMBER_STRING = 'FY2026'
      GROUP BY s.STAGE_NAME, s.SORT_ORDER
      ORDER BY s.SORT_ORDER;

  - name: dedup_vs_raw_comparison
    question: How much double-counting does the deduplication remove for FY26?
    sql: |
      WITH raw AS (
        SELECT SUM(FORECASTED_HOURS) AS raw_hours
        FROM __fact_forecast_booking f
        JOIN __dim_date d ON f.DIM_DATE_SID = d.DIM_DATE_SID
        WHERE d.FY_NUMBER_STRING = 'FY2026'
      ),
      dedup AS (
        SELECT SUM(FORECASTED_HOURS) AS dedup_hours
        FROM (
          SELECT FORECASTED_HOURS
          FROM __fact_forecast_booking f
          JOIN __dim_date d ON f.DIM_DATE_SID = d.DIM_DATE_SID
          WHERE d.FY_NUMBER_STRING = 'FY2026'
          QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY f.DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID, f.DIM_DATE_SID, f.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
            ORDER BY f.EFFECTIVE_FROM DESC
          ) = 1
        )
      )
      SELECT raw.raw_hours, dedup.dedup_hours, (raw.raw_hours - dedup.dedup_hours) AS removed_duplicate_hours
      FROM raw, dedup;

  - name: per_employee_fte_next_90_days
    question: What is the per-employee booked FTE over the next 90 days (deduplicated)?
    sql: |
      WITH dedup AS (
        SELECT DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID, DIM_DATE_SID, DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID, FTE
        FROM __fact_forecast_booking
        QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
          PARTITION BY DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID, DIM_DATE_SID, DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
          ORDER BY EFFECTIVE_FROM DESC
        ) = 1
      )
      SELECT
        e.FIRST_NAME || ' ' || e.LAST_NAME  AS employee,
        AVG(f.FTE)                          AS avg_fte_next_90d
      FROM dedup f
      JOIN __dim_employee e
        ON f.DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID = e.DIM_EMPLOYEE_SID
      JOIN __dim_date d
        ON f.DIM_DATE_SID = d.DIM_DATE_SID
      WHERE d.DATE BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE() AND DATEADD('DAY', 90, CURRENT_DATE())
      GROUP BY e.FIRST_NAME, e.LAST_NAME
      ORDER BY avg_fte_next_90d DESC NULLS LAST;
{% endset %}
{{ return(yaml_content) }}
{% endmacro %}

macro.cr_project.sv_yaml_opportunity_fie.name: sv_yaml_opportunity_field_history
macro.cr_project.sv_yaml_opportunity_fie.macro_sql:
{% macro sv_yaml_opportunity_field_history() %}
{% set yaml_content %}
name: opportunity_field_history
description: >
  Historical tracking of Salesforce opportunity field changes including deal value (Amount),
  stage name, start date, and end date. Each row represents the latest snapshot of an
  opportunity's tracked fields for a given day, sourced from Salesforce field history.

module_custom_instructions:
  sql_generation: |
    - Only use the logical tables and columns defined in this semantic model.
    - The amount, start_date, and end_date columns are stored as VARCHAR from Salesforce field history pivoting.
      Use TRY_CAST(amount AS NUMBER(18,2)) and TRY_CAST(start_date AS DATE) / TRY_CAST(end_date AS DATE) when filtering or aggregating.
    - Stage ordering (sales pipeline progression):
        1 = Prospecting
        2 = Qualifying
        3 = Validating
        4 = Best Case
        5 = Commit
        6 = Closed Won
      Negative outcome: Closed Lost (treated as 0 or -1 for ordering).
      Use a CASE expression to map stage_name -> stage_order for numeric comparison.
    - "Pipeline movement" or "pipeline changes" means stage transitions.
      Compare an opportunity's previous stage to its current stage using LAG or self-joins
      on opportunity_bk ordered by created_date. A positive movement is stage_order increasing
      (progressing toward Closed Won). A negative movement is stage_order decreasing or
      moving to Closed Lost.
    - "Drivers of pipeline movement" means the stage transitions (from_stage -> to_stage) that
      are most common or that carry the highest deal value. Group by the transition pair and
      aggregate by count or sum of amount.
    - When the user asks to include opportunity names, dates, amounts, or other details for the top drivers,
      do not concatenate detail values into a single LISTAGG or string column. First identify the top transition
      groups, then return the detailed transition rows with separate columns such as opportunity_name,
      service_offering, customer_lead_name, transition_date, and amount.
    - For requests like "top drivers ... including details", return one row per opportunity transition detail,
      repeating the grouped driver columns alongside the detail columns.
    - "What moves opps up stages faster" means measuring the time (days) an opportunity spends
      in each stage before progressing. Shorter dwell time = faster progression.
    - When asked about "this week", use DATE_TRUNC('WEEK', CURRENT_DATE()) as the week start.
    - When asked about "last two weeks" or "past 14 days", use CREATED_DATE >= DATEADD('day', -14, CURRENT_DATE())
      and CREATED_DATE <= CURRENT_DATE().
    - dim_opportunity_sid can be joined to dim_opportunity for opportunity name, service offering,
      forecast category, deal value, type, customer lead, partners, etc.
    - dim_stage provides the canonical stage ordering via sort_order and probability %.
      Prefer joining to dim_stage on stage_name rather than hardcoding stage sequences.
      Use dim_stage.sort_order for numeric stage comparisons and dim_stage.probability
      for weighted pipeline calculations.
    - Join paths:
        fact_opportunity_field_history.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID = dim_opportunity.DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
        fact_opportunity_field_history.STAGE_NAME = dim_stage.STAGE_NAME
    - Format all dollar/monetary columns using TO_VARCHAR(value, '$999,999,999,999.00') to display
      with a $ sign and comma-separated thousands.

tables:

  - name: fact_opportunity_field_history
    description: >
      Daily snapshots of Salesforce opportunity field changes. Tracks Amount, StageName,
      Start_Date, and End_Date fields. One row per opportunity per day with the latest
      values as of that day.
    base_table:
      database: __TARGET_DATABASE__
      schema: __TARGET_SCHEMA__
      table: FACT_OPPORTUNITY_FIELD_HISTORY

    dimensions:

      - name: dim_opportunity_sid
        description: Surrogate ID for the opportunity, joins to dim_opportunity.
        expr: DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
        data_type: TEXT
        synonyms:
          - opportunity sid
          - opportunity surrogate id

      - name: dim_date_sid__created_date
        description: Surrogate ID for the created date, joins to dim_date.
        expr: DIM_DATE_SID__CREATED_DATE

        synonyms:
          - date sid
          - date surrogate id

      - name: opportunity_bk
        description: Business key uniquely identifying the Salesforce opportunity.
        expr: OPPORTUNITY_BK
        data_type: TEXT
        synonyms:
          - opportunity id
          - opportunity key
          - opp id
          - salesforce opportunity id

      - name: created_by_id
        description: Salesforce user ID of the person who made the field change.
        expr: CREATED_BY_ID
        data_type: TEXT
        synonyms:
          - changed by
          - modified by
          - user id

      - name: stage_name
        description: >
          The opportunity stage as of this snapshot. Stages follow the sales pipeline
          progression: Prospecting -> Qualifying -> Validating -> Best Case -> Commit ->
          Closed Won. Negative outcome: Closed Lost. NULL if stage was not changed
          on this date.
        expr: STAGE_NAME
        data_type: TEXT
        synonyms:
          - stage
          - pipeline stage
          - opportunity stage
          - sales stage
        sample_values:
          - Prospecting
          - Qualifying
          - Validating
          - Best Case
          - Commit
          - Closed Won
          - Closed Lost
        is_enum: true

      - name: record_source
        description: Source system identifier (SALESFORCE).
        expr: RECORD_SOURCE
        data_type: TEXT
        synonyms:
          - source
          - source system

    time_dimensions:

      - name: created_date
        description: Date/time when the field change was recorded in Salesforce.
        expr: CREATED_DATE
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        synonyms:
          - change date
          - modified date
          - when changed
          - snapshot date

      - name: load_date_time
        description: Timestamp when the record was loaded into the warehouse.
        expr: LOAD_DATE_TIME
        data_type: TIMESTAMP
        synonyms:
          - loaded at
          - refresh timestamp

      - name: start_date
        description: >
          The opportunity's projected start date as of this snapshot. Stored as VARCHAR;
          cast to DATE for filtering.
        expr: TRY_CAST(START_DATE AS DATE)
        data_type: DATE
        synonyms:
          - project start
          - engagement start
          - opp start date

      - name: end_date
        description: >
          The opportunity's projected end date as of this snapshot. Stored as VARCHAR;
          cast to DATE for filtering.
        expr: TRY_CAST(END_DATE AS DATE)
        data_type: DATE
        synonyms:
          - project end
          - engagement end
          - opp end date

    facts:

      - name: amount
        description: >
          The opportunity deal value as of this snapshot. Stored as VARCHAR from Salesforce
          field history; cast to NUMBER for aggregation.
        expr: TRY_CAST(AMOUNT AS NUMBER(18,2))
        data_type: NUMBER
        synonyms:
          - deal value
          - opportunity amount
          - pipeline value
          - value
          - dollar amount

    metrics:

      - name: total_pipeline_value
        description: Sum of opportunity amounts across the current filter context.
        expr: SUM(amount)
        synonyms:
          - total deal value
          - total pipeline
          - pipeline total

      - name: average_deal_value
        description: Average opportunity amount across the current filter context.
        expr: AVG(amount)
        synonyms:
          - avg deal value
          - average amount

      - name: opportunity_count
        description: Count of distinct opportunities.
        expr: COUNT(DISTINCT opportunity_bk)
        synonyms:
          - number of opportunities
          - opp count
          - deal count

  - name: dim_opportunity
    description: >
      Opportunity dimension from Salesforce. Contains opportunity attributes including

    base_table:
      database: __TARGET_DATABASE__

    dimensions:

        expr: DIM_OPPORTUNITY_SID
        data_type: TEXT
        unique: true
        synonyms:
          - opportunity sid

      - name: opportunity_bk
        description: Salesforce opportunity business key.
        expr: OPPORTUNITY_BK
        data_type: TEXT
        unique: true
        synonyms:
          - opportunity id
          - opp id

      - name: opportunity_name
        description: Human-readable name of the opportunity.
        expr: OPPORTUNITY_NAME
        data_type: TEXT
        synonyms:
          - opportunity
          - opp name
          - deal name

      - name: service_offering

        expr: SERVICE_OFFERING

      - name: third_party_product
